patch_description:
The current program uses excessive parameter sharing in the ansatz (only 74 total params) which reduces expressivity despite faster convergence. The prior programs achieved 0.87 test accuracy with 98 parameters using more individual parameters in input/output layers plus mirror-symmetry sharing.

Key improvements:
1. **Richer Ansatz**: Restore individual RY input parameters (8 params) instead of just 2 shared params; keep ring CRX connectivity but with 4 mirror-shared params instead of 8 unique; add 4 mirror-shared RZ params and 4 mirror-shared output RY params. This yields ~20 params/block × 6 blocks = 120 circuit params.

2. **Mirror-Pair Readout Calibration**: Replace global gain/bias (2 params) with per-mirror-pair calibration (8 params). After computing 8 Z-expectations, average them over pairs (0&7), (1&6), (2&5), (3&4) to get 4 values, then apply independent gain_i/bias_i to each pair before taking the final mean. This finer-grained calibration mirrors the ansatz symmetry and should improve convergence speed while maintaining per-block parameter efficiency.

Target: ~128 total parameters, better than current 74 (too sparse) but close to prior 98 (which had good generalization), with tighter train-test gap via symmetric readout.
